definitions.name: Cumulant-separated non-Gaussian PLM uncertainty class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}=\{P: \eta\perp X,\ E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\), where \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) are the residual functionals already defined from \(P\).

definitions.name: Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis bounded-outcome Gaussian uncertainty class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}=\{P:E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ |Y|\le C_q,\ \eta\perp X,\ \eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2),\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\) within the published PLM, with \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) given by their displayed residual definitions. This is exactly the bounded-outcome class intersected with the known-variance Gaussian and supplied-code restrictions in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.

definitions.name: Published sub-Gaussian ACE comparator class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}=\{P:E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\ |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\ \|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\ \|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\ \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\ \|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\ \eta\perp X,\ |\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\ \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\}\), with the residual functionals defined from \(P\).

definitions.name: Multiplicity-adjusted transform-zero instrument
definitions.construction: Given a zero \(z_0\) of \(M\) with multiplicity \(\ell\), set \(J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}e^{z_0w}\).

definitions.name: Observable contour functional
definitions.construction: For a positively oriented circle \(C_j\) on which \(F_n\) is zero-free and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\), set \(\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)=\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_j}G_n(z)/F_n(z)\,dz\).

definitions.name: Compact-open contour-bank construction
definitions.construction: Take the locally uniform closure of the centered sub-Gaussian MGFs satisfying \(|\kappa_k|\ge\delta\); for each member choose a rational radius in \((R_0,R_1)\) avoiding its zeros, use Rouche stability to form a compact-open neighborhood preserving positive zero count and boundary separation, extract a finite subcover, retain its radii \(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_J\), and define \(a_{\star}\) as one half of the smallest retained boundary modulus.

definitions.name: Adaptive split-sample contour estimator
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat F_{a,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{a,n}\) on \(I_a\). Declare \(j\) pilot-admissible when \(\inf_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}(z)|\ge a_{\star}/2\) and \(\widehat N_{0j,n}\ge1\). Let \(\widehat j_n\) be the smallest maximizer of the pilot boundary modulus over admissible indices. Return zero if the set is empty or if \(\inf_{z\in C_{\widehat j_n}}|\widehat F_{1,n}(z)|<a_{\star}/4\); otherwise return \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}=\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}\operatorname{Re}[\{\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_{\widehat j_n}}\widehat G_{1,n}(z)/\widehat F_{1,n}(z)\,dz]\). Ties and failure events use the displayed deterministic rules, making the finite-bank selector measurable once the contour integrals are represented by fixed parametrizations.

definitions.name: Common-code minimax losses
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]\), \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]\), and \(\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)|)\).

definitions.name: Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4 eligibility
definitions.construction: Compute \(a_{1,n},b_{1,n},a_2,b_{2,n}\) exactly as in condition (21) and set \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) to the condition \(r\le\min\{b_{1,n}/a_{1,n}-a_{1,n}^{-1}\log(b_{1,n}/a_{1,n}),b_{2,n}/[a_2\log(a_2b_{2,n})]\}\) on indices for which these expressions are defined.

definitions.name: Symmetric-mixture sine estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}=\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}\{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(\pi Z_n/2)]/\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(\pi Z_n/2)]\}\), with fallback zero when the empirical denominator is below one half of its population lower bound.

definitions.name: Weak-spectral-information construction handle
definitions.construction: Starting from a growing rational library of complex circles, estimate on independent folds each circle's winding number, boundary modulus, and contour-moment variance; use these observable strength diagnostics to construct \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}\) by weak-identification-robust switching among DML, finite-order ACE, and contour moments, and derive the critical scaling when \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\downarrow0\).

statements.statement: If \(z_0\) is a zero of \(M\) of multiplicity \(\ell\), then for every real shift \(d\), \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]=0\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), this gives \(E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]=0\) and \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]=M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0)\); whenever this value is nonzero, \(\theta_0=E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]/E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\).
statements.justification: This exact identity displays the global location-family null score and its relevance under residual contamination.
statements.gap: Transform-zero incompleteness is classical, but its multiplicity-adjusted score has not been used to eliminate an arbitrary PLM covariate shift created by a supplied treatment code.
statements.consumer: Known-noise implementations can estimate the causal coefficient by a single bounded or exponentially weighted moment ratio.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a zero \(z_0\) of multiplicity \(\ell\).  Since \(M\) is an entire moment transform, differentiation under the expectation is valid and, for every integer \(j\geq 0\),
\[
M^{(j)}(z)=E_P\!\left[\eta^j e^{z\eta}\right].
\]
Indeed, for \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), sub-Gaussianity of \(\eta\) gives finite exponential moments of every real order and hence an integrable dominating function for each derivative on every compact subset of \(\mathbb C\).  The multiplicity condition is therefore
\[
M^{(j)}(z_0)=0\quad(0\leq j<\ell),
\qquad
M^{(\ell)}(z_0)\neq 0.
\]
For an arbitrary real \(d\), the binomial identity gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)\right]
&=E_P\!\left[(\eta+d)^{\ell-1}e^{z_0(\eta+d)}\right]\\
&=e^{z_0d}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
  {\ell-1\choose j}d^{\ell-1-j}
  E_P\!\left[\eta^j e^{z_0\eta}\right]\\
&=e^{z_0d}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}
  {\ell-1\choose j}d^{\ell-1-j}M^{(j)}(z_0)
=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves exact annihilation for every shift, including shifts on the boundary of the support of \(D_n\); no support-interior or overlap condition is used.

Now fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  The random variable \(D_n=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), and \(\eta\perp X\).  Thus the conditional law of \(\eta\) given \(X\) equals its marginal law, and substitution of \(d=D_n\) in the preceding identity yields, componentwise for the complex conditional expectation,
\[
E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X\right]
=E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+D_n)\mid X\right]
=0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Applying the same calculation with exponent \(\ell\) rather than \(\ell-1\), and again conditioning on \(X\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P\!\left[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X\right]
&=E_P\!\left[(\eta+D_n)^\ell e^{z_0(\eta+D_n)}\mid X\right]\\
&=e^{z_0D_n}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}{\ell\choose j}
  D_n^{\ell-j}M^{(j)}(z_0)\\
&=e^{z_0D_n}M^{(\ell)}(z_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking expectations and using the definition \(H_n(z)=E_P[e^{zD_n}]\),
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]
=M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\]

It remains to establish the outcome moment.  From the residual decomposition,
\[
Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi.
\]
The first contamination term vanishes by the conditional annihilation already proved:
\[
E_P\!\left[b_n(X)J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]
=E_P\!\left[b_n(X)E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X\right]\right]
=0.
\]
Because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), the variable \(J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(X,T)\).  The outcome mean-independence assumption consequently gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P\!\left[\xi J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]
&=E_P\!\left[
J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)E_P[\xi\mid X,T]
\right]
=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
E_P\!\left[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]
=\theta_0E_P\!\left[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right].
\]
Whenever \(M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0)\neq0\), division is valid and proves
\[
\theta_0
=\frac{E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}
       {E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}.
\]
This ratio is an observed-population functional because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) and the instrument is fixed once \((z_0,\ell)\) is supplied; its equality to the causal coefficient uses the independent-treatment-noise and outcome mean-independence assumptions.  All displayed expectations are finite: \(|D_n|\leq2C_g\), \(b_n\) is bounded, and the sub-Gaussian bounds on \(\eta\) and \(\xi\) dominate every fixed complex-exponential polynomial weight appearing above.  The sole rank condition is the explicitly stated nonvanishing denominator; no positivity or treatment-overlap condition is required.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)\) and \(G_n(z)=\theta_0F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).
statements.justification: The identity recovers the latent transform-zero geometry from observable learned residuals and isolates an analytic nuisance ratio.
statements.gap: Classical convolution results do not provide the outcome transform \(G_n=\theta_0F_n'+MB_n\) for a partially linear causal coefficient.
statements.consumer: The contour theorem integrates \(G_n/F_n\) and removes \(B_n/H_n\) exactly.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  By the definitions of \(D_n\) and \(Z_n\),
\[
 Z_n=\eta+D_n,
\]
where \(D_n\) is measurable with respect to \(X\).  The independence restriction \(\eta\perp X\) therefore gives, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
 F_n(z)
 =E_P[e^{z(\eta+D_n)}]
 =E_P[e^{z\eta}]E_P[e^{zD_n}]
 =M(z)H_n(z).
\]
All expectations are finite: \(D_n\) is bounded by \(2C_g\), while sub-Gaussianity of \(\eta\) gives finite exponential moments of every real order.  The same bounds justify differentiation under the expectation, so
\[
 F_n'(z)=E_P[Z_ne^{zZ_n}].
\]
The residual identity in the symbol definitions is
\[
 Y=\theta_0Z_n+b_n(X)+\xi.
\]
Because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), outcome mean independence yields
\[
 E_P[\xi e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P\!\left[e^{zZ_n}E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\right]
 =0.
\]
Independence of \(\eta\) and \(X\) also gives
\[
 E_P[b_n(X)e^{zZ_n}]
 =E_P[e^{z\eta}]E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}]
 =M(z)B_n(z).
\]
Combining the last three displays proves
\[
 G_n(z)=E_P[Ye^{zZ_n}]=\theta_0F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z).
\]
The domination already noted also shows that all four transforms in the identities are entire.

statements.statement: Let \(C_j\) be positively oriented. If \(F_n\) is zero-free on \(C_j\), \(H_n\) is zero-free on and inside \(C_j\), and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\), then \(\theta_0=\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)=\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}\oint_{C_j}G_n(z)/F_n(z)\,dz\).
statements.justification: The observable contour formula identifies the coefficient without learning the outcome regression or separating the two transform factors.
statements.gap: Location-family completeness and real-zero tests do not construct this observable complex contour functional for a PLM coefficient.
statements.consumer: The adaptive estimator evaluates the identifying functional on a pilot-selected contour.
statements.proof_tex:
On \(C_j\), the factorization lemma and the assumed absence of zeros give
\[
 \frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}
 =\theta_0\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}+\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}.
\]
The functions \(B_n\) and \(H_n\) are entire.  Since \(H_n\) is zero-free on and inside \(C_j\), the quotient \(B_n/H_n\) is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk bounded by \(C_j\).  The Cauchy integral identity therefore gives
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{B_n(z)}{H_n(z)}\,dz=0.
\]
By the definition of \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\),
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{F_n'(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz=N_{C_j}(F_n).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 =\theta_0N_{C_j}(F_n).
\]
The assumed positivity \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\) permits division.  The result is exactly
\[
 \theta_0
 =\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}
   \oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz
 =\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n).
\]
Thus the causal coefficient is distinct from, but under the displayed conditions equal to, the computable observed-transform contour functional.

statements.statement: There is \(A_k<\infty\), depending only on \(k\), such that every centered law with \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta\) has a zero of \(M\) in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\), where \(R_0\le A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}\).
statements.justification: A uniform estimator requires usable spectral information in a disk fixed by primitive class constants.
statements.gap: Quantitative Marcinkiewicz results control Gaussian approximation from zero-free disks; this converse direction localizes a zero from fixed cumulant separation.
statements.consumer: The contour bank only searches the fixed disk determined here.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(c_{\psi}<\infty\) be the universal constant in the moment-generating-function consequence of the \(\psi_2\) bound:
\[
 E_P[e^{t\eta}]\le \exp(c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}t^{2}),
 \qquad t\in\mathbb R.
\]
This follows directly by expanding the exponential and using the sub-Gaussian moment bounds \(\|\eta\|_{L^p}\le C\psi_{\eta}\sqrt p\).  Hence, for complex \(z\),
\[
 |M(z)|\le E_P[e^{\operatorname{Re}(z)\eta}]
 \le \exp(c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}|z|^{2}).
\]

Fix \(R>0\) and suppose, toward a contradiction, that \(M\) has no zero in \(\{|z|\le R\}\).  Since the disk is simply connected and \(M(0)=1\), there is an analytic logarithm \(K=\log M\) on a neighborhood of the disk, normalized by \(K(0)=0\).  Put \(A=c_{\psi}\psi_{\eta}^{2}R^{2}\).  The preceding display implies
\[
 \operatorname{Re}K(z)=\log|M(z)|\le A,
 \qquad |z|\le R.
\]
For completeness, the needed analytic bound follows without an additional probabilistic assumption.  The function
\[
 h(z)=\frac{K(z)}{2A-K(z)}
\]
satisfies \(|h(z)|\le1\), because
\[
 |2A-K(z)|^{2}-|K(z)|^{2}
 =4A\{A-\operatorname{Re}K(z)\}\ge0,
\]
and \(h(0)=0\).  Applying the Schwarz inequality after rescaling the radius-
\(R\) disk gives \(|h(z)|\le |z|/R\).  Thus, for \(|z|\le R/2\),
\[
 |K(z)|\le \frac{2A(|z|/R)}{1-|z|/R}\le2A.
\]
The Cauchy coefficient formula on \(|z|=R/2\) now yields
\[
 |\kappa_k(\eta)|=|K^{(k)}(0)|
 \le k!\frac{2A}{(R/2)^k}
 =2^{k+1}c_{\psi}k!\,\psi_{\eta}^{2}R^{2-k}.
\]
Choose
\[
 A_k=(2^{k+2}c_{\psi}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 R_0=A_k(\psi_{\eta}^{2}/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}.
\]
If \(M\) were zero-free on the radius-\(R_0\) disk, the preceding inequality would give \(|\kappa_k(\eta)|\le\delta/2\), contradicting cumulant separation.  Therefore \(M\) has a zero with \(|z|\le R_0\).  This choice has the asserted dependence and, in particular, \(R_0\le A_k(\psi_{\eta}^{2}/\delta)^{1/(k-2)}\), with equality for the displayed choice.

statements.statement: The construction in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\) yields finite \(J\), radii \(R_0<\rho_j<R_1\), and \(a_{\star}>0\) such that every treatment-noise transform represented in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) has some \(j\) with \(N_{C_j}(M)\ge1\) and \(\inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}\). The conclusion is uniform in \(n\).
statements.justification: Pointwise zero existence does not imply uniform risk; compact-open closure and boundary stability must produce a finite conditioned bank.
statements.gap: Existing pointwise transform-zero theory and zero-free-disk inequalities do not establish a finite contour cover uniform over this cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian class.
statements.consumer: A finite bank makes selection measurable and reduces stochastic control to finitely many contour ratios.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr K\) be the locally uniform closure appearing in \(\text{def:contour-bank-handle}\).  We first verify its compactness and that the defining restrictions survive closure.  Uniform sub-Gaussianity gives constants \(c,C>0\), depending only on \(\psi_{\eta}\), such that every underlying law satisfies
\[
 P(|\eta|>u)\le C e^{-cu^2/\psi_{\eta}^{2}}.
\]
Thus the laws are uniformly tight.  From any sequence one obtains a weakly convergent subsequence by diagonal extraction of the distribution functions at rational continuity points.  The same tail bound implies uniform integrability of \(e^{S|\eta|}\) for each fixed \(S<\infty\).  Truncation at \(|\eta|\le L\), followed by weak convergence and then \(L\to\infty\), shows pointwise convergence of the MGFs on \(\mathbb C\).  The derivative envelope
\[
 \sup E_P[|\eta|e^{S|\eta|}]<\infty
\]
makes the transforms equicontinuous on \(\{|z|\le S\}\); hence the convergence is locally uniform.  The same uniform-integrability argument applies to every moment, so centering and \(|\kappa_k|\ge\delta\) pass to the limit.  The \(\psi_2\) bound passes by Fatou's inequality.  Therefore \(\mathscr K\) is sequentially compact in the metrizable compact-open topology and hence compact.

Fix \(M\in\mathscr K\).  The zero-localization lemma gives a zero in \(\{|z|\le R_0\}\).  Since \(M(0)=1\), \(M\) is not identically zero, and its zeros are isolated.  We may therefore choose a rational \(\rho(M)\in(R_0,R_1)\) whose circle contains no zero.  Set
\[
 m(M)=\inf_{|z|=\rho(M)}|M(z)|>0.
\]
The circle encloses at least the localized zero.  Factoring the finitely many enclosed zeros with their multiplicities and applying the Cauchy coefficient identity to the remaining zero-free analytic factor gives
\[
 \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z|=\rho(M)}\frac{M'(z)}{M(z)}\,dz
 =N_{|z|=\rho(M)}(M)\ge1.
\]

Consider the compact-open neighborhood
\[
 \mathscr U_M
 =\left\{\widetilde M\in\mathscr K:
   \sup_{|z|=\rho(M)}|\widetilde M(z)-M(z)|<m(M)/2\right\}.
\]
Every \(\widetilde M\in\mathscr U_M\) has boundary modulus at least \(m(M)/2\).  Moreover the homotopy \(M_t=(1-t)M+t\widetilde M\) is zero-free on that circle for every \(t\in[0,1]\).  The integral
\[
 t\longmapsto \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z|=\rho(M)}\frac{M_t'(z)}{M_t(z)}\,dz
\]
is continuous and integer-valued, so it is constant.  Hence every member of \(\mathscr U_M\) has the same positive enclosed zero count as \(M\).

The neighborhoods \(\{\mathscr U_M:M\in\mathscr K\}\) cover the compact set \(\mathscr K\).  Choose a finite subcover \(\mathscr U_{M_1},\ldots,\mathscr U_{M_J}\), put
\[
 \rho_j=\rho(M_j),
 \qquad
 a_{\star}=\frac12\min_{1\le j\le J}m(M_j)>0,
\]
and let \(C_j=\{|z|=\rho_j\}\).  Any admissible treatment transform belongs to some \(\mathscr U_{M_j}\), and for that \(j\),
\[
 N_{C_j}(M)\ge1,
 \qquad
 \inf_{z\in C_j}|M(z)|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
Only the fixed class constants enter \(\mathscr K\), so \(J\), the radii, and \(a_{\star}\) do not depend on \(n\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), clipping and \(L^s(P_X)\) control imply \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) and \(E_P|D_n|\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Hence \(\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|H_n(z)-1|\le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}\). If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), then \(|H_n(z)|\ge3/4\) on the disk, and \(F_n=M H_n\) and \(M\) have the same zeros there with multiplicity.
statements.justification: This quantitative stability step prevents learned-residual contamination from adding or removing poles inside the selected contour.
statements.gap: Published zero-inheritance arguments assume exact additive independence and do not bound a learned-residual contamination factor at fixed nonzero code error.
statements.consumer: The adaptive risk theorem transfers the latent contour bank to the observable transform.
statements.proof_tex:
Because both \(g_0\) and \(\bar g_n\) take values in \([-C_g,C_g]\),
\[
 |D_n|=|g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)|\le2C_g
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Since \(P_X\) is a probability law and \(s\ge r+1\ge1\), Lyapunov's inequality and the treatment-code-radius assumption give
\[
 E_P|D_n|=\|g_0-\bar g_n\|_{L^1(P_X)}
 \le\|g_0-\bar g_n\|_{L^s(P_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
For arbitrary complex \(w\), the identity
\[
 e^w-1=w\int_0^1e^{tw}\,dt
\]
implies \(|e^w-1|\le |w|e^{|w|}\).  Therefore, uniformly over \(|z|\le R_1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |H_n(z)-1|
 &\le E_P|e^{zD_n}-1|\\
 &\le |z|E_P[|D_n|e^{|z||D_n|}]\\
 &\le R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0=\{4R_1e^{2C_gR_1}\}^{-1}\), then this bound is at most \(1/4\), whence
\[
 |H_n(z)|\ge1-|H_n(z)-1|\ge3/4
 \qquad (|z|\le R_1).
\]
Thus \(H_n\) has no zero in the disk.  By observable factorization, \(F_n=M H_n\); multiplication by a nonvanishing analytic function neither creates a zero nor changes its multiplicity.  Hence \(F_n\) and \(M\) have exactly the same zeros there, counted with multiplicity.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), then it contains a one-dimensional submodel \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) with the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0,q_0,\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), independent Gaussian outcome innovation of fixed positive variance not exceeding the \(\psi_{\xi}\) envelope, and \(Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star}\). For \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})\le C_0h^2\), where \(c_0,C_0\) depend only on fixed class constants.
statements.justification: The parametric lower bound must exhibit a class member while preserving the supplied codes and both uncertainty balls.
statements.gap: A generic appeal to a parametric submodel does not verify membership in a triangular common-code class.
statements.consumer: Le Cam's two-point lemma turns this construction into the \(c/n\) half of the spectral minimax rate.
statements.proof_tex:
Choose any \(P_{n,\star}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), and retain from it the joint law of \((X,T)\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\), and the treatment noise \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\).  Choose \(\tau>0\), depending only on \(\psi_{\xi}\), so small that a centered \(N(0,\tau^2)\) variable has \(\psi_2\)-norm at most \(\psi_{\xi}\).  Let \(\xi_{\star}\sim N(0,\tau^2)\) be independent of \((X,T)\), and put
\[
 c_0=\min\{C_{\theta}/2,1\}>0,
 \qquad
 Y_{\vartheta}=q_0(X)+\vartheta\eta+\xi_{\star},
 \qquad |\vartheta|\le c_0.
\]
Denote the resulting law by \(P_{n,\vartheta}\).  Since \(\eta\perp X\) and \(E_P\eta=0\),
\[
 E_{P_{n,\vartheta}}[Y_{\vartheta}\mid X]=q_0(X).
\]
The residual outcome innovation under parameter \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\) is exactly \(\xi_{\star}\), and
\[
 E[\xi_{\star}\mid X,T]=0,
 \qquad
 \|\xi_{\star}\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}.
\]
All treatment-side restrictions, the cumulant separation, and the treatment-code radius are unchanged.  The outcome regression \(q_0\), and therefore its range and its distance from the fixed code \(\bar q_n\), is also unchanged.  Finally \(|\vartheta|\le C_{\theta}\).  Hence every \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), with the asserted common objects.

Conditional on \((X,T)\), the two outcome laws at \(\vartheta_0\) and \(\vartheta_1\) are normal with common variance \(\tau^2\) and means differing by \((\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)\eta\).  Thus
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1})
 =\frac{(\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0)^2}{2\tau^2}E_P[\eta^2].
\]
The treatment sub-Gaussian bound implies \(E_P[\eta^2]\le C\psi_{\eta}^2\).  Additivity of relative entropy for independent products therefore gives, when \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\|P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})
 =\frac{h^2}{2\tau^2}E_P[\eta^2]
 \le C_0h^2,
\]
where \(C_0\) depends only on \(\psi_{\eta}\) and \(\psi_{\xi}\).

statements.statement: For \(n\ge2\), suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\). There are \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), such that \(c/n\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]\le C/n\), uniformly over every deterministic nested \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). The estimator uses \(\bar g_n\), does not use \(\bar q_n\), and does not know the law of \(\eta\). Its MSE bound implies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|)\le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}\). On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), for every sequence of indices satisfying \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), this removes the two nuisance terms in Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis bound (22); whenever \(\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}+C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\gg n^{-1/2}\), the spectral generalized-quantile guarantee is strictly smaller in order than \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\).
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the proposed statement, which adds only the necessary boundary condition \(n\ge2\).

\emph{Upper bound.}
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  By the finite-contour-bank lemma there is an index \(j_0\) such that
\[
 N_{C_{j_0}}(M)\ge1,
 \qquad
 \inf_{C_{j_0}}|M|\ge a_{\star}.
\]
The nuisance-zero-free lemma and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\) imply that \(|H_n|\ge3/4\) on the bank disk and that \(F_n\) and \(M\) have the same zeros there.  Therefore
\[
 N_{C_{j_0}}(F_n)\ge1,
 \qquad
 \inf_{C_{j_0}}|F_n|\ge3a_{\star}/4.
\]
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 \Delta_{F,a}=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|,
 \qquad
 \Delta_{G,a}=\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|.
\]
Let
\[
 \mathcal E=\{\Delta_{F,0}\le a_{\star}/8,\ \Delta_{F,1}\le a_{\star}/8\}.
\]
Since both half-sample sizes are bounded below by a fixed multiple of \(n\) for \(n\ge2\), the empirical-transform lemma and Markov's inequality give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}P(\mathcal E^c)\le K/n.
\]

On \(\mathcal E\), the favorable contour \(j_0\) has pilot boundary modulus at least \(5a_{\star}/8\).  The straight-line homotopy between \(F_n\) and \(\widehat F_{0,n}\) is zero-free on that boundary, so their winding numbers agree and \(j_0\) is pilot-admissible.  By the maximizing rule, the selected index \(\widehat j_n\) satisfies
\[
 \inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|\widehat F_{0,n}|
 \ge5a_{\star}/8.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|F_n|\ge a_{\star}/2,
 \qquad
 \widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}=N_{C_{\widehat j_n}}(F_n)\ge1.
\]
The evaluation transform then obeys
\[
 \inf_{C_{\widehat j_n}}|\widehat F_{1,n}|
 \ge3a_{\star}/8>a_{\star}/4,
\]
so the evaluation fallback is not used.  This also proves measurability of the operational selection: the bank is finite, each boundary infimum equals the infimum over a fixed countable dense parametrization of its circle, the contour integrals use fixed parametrizations, and ties are deterministic.

The exact-contour theorem applies on the selected contour.  Put \(N=N_{C_{\widehat j_n}}(F_n)=\widehat N_{0\widehat j_n,n}\).  Uniformly over the class and the bank,
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|G_n(z)|
 \le E_P[|Y|e^{R_1|Z_n|}]\le K_G<\infty,
\]
because \(Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta+\xi\), \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), and \(\eta,\xi\) have the stated sub-Gaussian envelopes.  Since \(N\ge1\) and every bank circle has radius at most \(R_1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|\frac{1}{N2\pi i}\oint_{C_{\widehat j_n}}
 \left\{\frac{\widehat G_{1,n}}{\widehat F_{1,n}}-
 \frac{G_n}{F_n}\right\}\,dz\right|\\
 &\quad\le R_1\left\{
 \frac{8}{3a_{\star}}\Delta_{G,1}
 +\frac{16K_G}{3a_{\star}^{2}}\Delta_{F,1}
 \right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) and taking real parts cannot increase distance from the real number \(\theta_0\).  The exact-contour identity and the empirical-transform lemma therefore imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0)^2\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E}]
 \le K/n.
\]
On \(\mathcal E^c\), both the estimator and the target lie in \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\), so the squared loss is at most \(4C_{\theta}^2\).  Combining this fact with the probability bound for \(\mathcal E^c\) proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \le C/n.
\]
The proof never uses \(\bar q_n\) or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\), and the finite bank depends on the class constants rather than the unknown law of \(\eta\).  Since the minimax infimum ranges over all data-dependent estimators using the common codes, this estimator is an admissible witness and
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
 \le \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2].
\]

\emph{Lower bound.}
Use the Gaussian-outcome submodel from \(\text{lem:non-gaussian-hard-submodel}\).  Take two parameters \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1\) in its interior with separation \(d=h/\sqrt n\), where \(h>0\) is a sufficiently small class-dependent constant.  Conditional on \((X,T)\), the outcome distributions are normals of common variance \(\tau^2\) and their means differ by \(d\eta\).  Their one-observation Hellinger affinity is
\[
 A_1=E_P\!\left[\exp\{-d^2\eta^2/(8\tau^2)\}\right]
 \ge\exp\{-d^2E_P[\eta^2]/(8\tau^2)\},
\]
where the inequality is Jensen's inequality.  Product structure and the uniform second-moment bound give
\[
 A_n=A_1^n\ge\exp\{-h^2C\psi_{\eta}^2/(8\tau^2)\}=:a_0>0.
\]
For densities \(p_0,p_1\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_1)
 \le\sqrt{1-\left(\int\sqrt{p_0p_1}\right)^2},
\]
so the sum of the two testing errors is at least
\[
 1-\operatorname{TV}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n},P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})
 \ge1-\sqrt{1-a_0^2}\ge a_0^2/2.
\]
Turning any estimator into the test that selects the closer of \(\vartheta_0\) and \(\vartheta_1\), at least one of its two squared risks is therefore at least
\[
 \frac{d^2}{8}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n},P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n})\}
 \ge \frac{h^2a_0^2}{16n}.
\]
Taking the infimum over estimators proves \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\ge c/n\).

\emph{Quantile and ACE comparison.}
For \(W=|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|\), Markov's inequality at \(t=\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}\) yields \(P(W>t)\le\gamma\).  Hence
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}}Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)
 \le\sqrt{C/(\gamma n)}.
\]
On the displayed class intersection and eligible indices, \(\text{lem:jms-ace-quantile-upper}\) supplies the published ACE guarantee.  Since \(6^r\le16^r\) and the coefficient \(4\) in its sampling term is at most \(64\), that published right-hand side is bounded above by \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\).  The spectral bound has no terms involving \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) or powers of \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\).  Finally, if
\[
 A_n=\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
 +C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}\gg n^{-1/2},
\]
then \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\ge c_1A_n\) while the spectral guarantee is \(O(n^{-1/2})\); their ratio is \(O(n^{-1/2}/A_n)=o(1)\).  This proves every clause of the proposed theorem.
statements.justification: This is the corrected theorem-level kernel: exact transform geometry, rather than a finite-cumulant converse, permits parametric risk at fixed treatment-code error.
statements.gap: Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4, condition (21), and bound (22) give a generalized-quantile ACE upper bound retaining two nuisance terms; no published result gives an unknown-noise contour estimator with uniform \(n^{-1}\) MSE at fixed nonzero treatment-code error.
statements.consumer: Demand estimation with separated non-Gaussian price shocks can retain parametric coefficient risk with a rough treatment learner and no outcome learner.

statements.statement: For \(s\ge r+1\), every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) satisfies the \(L^r(P_X)\) code controls needed to test membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), because \(\|f\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\|f\|_{L^s(P_X)}\). This norm implication does not identify the two base classes. If \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4 gives \(\sup_P Q_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|)\le B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\), with the supremum taken over that published uncertainty-class intersection.
statements.justification: The comparison must reproduce the published norm, eligibility condition, class intersection, quantile loss, and constants before any tightening claim is meaningful.
statements.gap: A rate-shape paraphrase suppresses condition (21), bound (22), and the difference between \(L^s\) control and literal equality of uncertainty classes.
statements.consumer: Referees can audit exactly which ACE-eligible sequences are strictly improved by the spectral theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  All norms below are
with respect to the probability measure \(P_X\).  The code errors are
measurable and bounded: \(g_0\) and \(\bar g_n\) take values in
\([-C_g,C_g]\), while \(q_0\) and \(\bar q_n\) take values in
\([-C_q,C_q]\).  Thus every norm and expectation used below is finite,
including at the endpoint \(s=\infty\).

First suppose \(r\le s<\infty\).  For any measurable \(f\), Jensen's
inequality for the concave map \(u\mapsto u^{r/s}\) on
\([0,\infty)\) gives
\[
 E_P[|f(X)|^r]
 =E_P\!\left[(|f(X)|^s)^{r/s}\right]
 \le \left(E_P[|f(X)|^s]\right)^{r/s}.
\]
Taking \(r\)-th roots yields
\[
 \|f\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le \|f\|_{L^s(P_X)}.                 \tag{1}
\]
If \(s=\infty\), then \(|f(X)|\le\|f\|_{L^\infty(P_X)}\)
almost surely, so integration and an \(r\)-th root give (1) again.
The standing range \(s\ge r+1\) in particular ensures \(s>r\), while
only \(s\ge r\) was needed for (1).

Apply (1) first to \(f=\bar g_n-g_0\) and then to
\(f=\bar q_n-q_0\).  The two \(L^s(P_X)\) restrictions in
\(\text{def:non-gaussian-class}\) imply
\[
 \|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
 \qquad
 \|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.       \tag{2}
\]
These are precisely the two code controls in
\(\text{def:jms-ace-class}\).  Every other member property displayed
in that definition is also a member property of
\(\text{def:non-gaussian-class}\).  Hence the definitions and (2) give
the one-way inclusion
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}
 \subseteq \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.   \tag{3}
\]
This does not identify the two classes as equal.  Indeed, norm
monotonicity has no converse with the same radius: on a probability
space containing an event \(A\) with \(0<P_X(A)<1\), the bounded
function \(f=c\mathbf 1_A\) satisfies
\[
 \frac{\|f\|_{L^s(P_X)}}{\|f\|_{L^r(P_X)}}
 =P_X(A)^{1/s-1/r}>1
\]
when \(s<\infty\), and the analogous ratio is
\(P_X(A)^{-1/r}>1\) when \(s=\infty\).  Thus (1) supplies only the
direction in (3); it does not supply equality of the uncertainty sets.

It remains to verify the displayed comparator bound, including its
constants.  Suppose \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds.  By
\(\text{def:jms-eligibility}\), all logarithms and divisions in
condition (21) are defined.  In particular, the case
\(\varepsilon_{1,n}=0\) is excluded whenever the antecedent holds.
Define the nonnegative proof intermediates
\[
 A_n=\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r}\varepsilon_{2,n}
       +C_\theta\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
\]
and
\[
 V_n=(C_g+\psi_\eta)^r
 \left\{r^2(C_g+\psi_\eta)+\psi_\xi+C_\theta\psi_\eta\right\}
 (\gamma n)^{-1/2}.
\]
The cited specialization \(\text{lem:jms-ace-theorem-five-four}\)
gives, for positive \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|\right)
 \le C_\gamma r!6^r\delta^{-1}(A_n+4V_n).                \tag{4}
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{2,n}=0\), apply the same cited theorem after replacing
that radius by an arbitrary \(u\in(0,\varepsilon_{1,n})\).  The original
radius-zero uncertainty set is contained in the radius-\(u\) set, and
the maximum defining \(b_{2,n}\) is unchanged, so the same eligibility
condition holds.  Taking the infimum of the resulting right-hand sides
over \(u\downarrow0\) proves (4) at the boundary as well.

Since \(A_n,V_n\ge0\), \(r\ge2\), \(6^r\le16^r\), and
\(A_n+4V_n\le A_n+64V_n\), equation (4) implies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \!\left(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|\right)
 \le C_\gamma r!16^r\delta^{-1}(A_n+64V_n)
 =B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}.                              \tag{5}
\]
The last equality is the definition of \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\).
The supremum in (5) is therefore over the published base-class and
\(L^r(P_X)\)-uncertainty intersection encoded by
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\); the deterministic
eligibility predicate is imposed at the displayed index \(n\), not
silently added as a property of an individual law.

statements.statement: Assume \(0<\varepsilon_{1,n}<1\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\varepsilon_{2,n}=o\{(\log n)^{-1/2}\}\). Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\), Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2 and equation (6), applied exactly to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), give \(\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}\ge L_{\mathrm G,n,\gamma}\). Under \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)=\inf\{t:P(W\le t)\ge1-\gamma\}\), the implication \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)\ge L\Rightarrow P(W\ge L)\ge\gamma\Rightarrow E_P[W^2]\ge\gamma L^2\) yields \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}\ge\gamma L_{\mathrm G,n,\gamma}^2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the proposed asymptotically qualified statement.  By \(\text{lem:jms-gaussian-quantile-lower}\), for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}\ge L_{\mathrm G,n,\gamma}.
\]
It remains to convert the loss without changing the experiment.  Let \(W\ge0\) and write
\[
 q=Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)=\inf\{t\ge0:P(W\le t)\ge1-\gamma\}.
\]
For every \(t<q\), \(P(W\le t)<1-\gamma\).  Letting \(t\uparrow q\) and using continuity from below gives
\[
 P(W<q)\le1-\gamma,
 \qquad
 P(W\ge q)\ge\gamma.
\]
Consequently
\[
 E_P[W^2]\ge q^2P(W\ge q)\ge\gamma q^2.
\]
Apply this inequality to the error of an arbitrary estimator \(\widetilde\theta\).  Taking the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) yields
\[
 \sup_P E_P[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2]
 \ge\gamma\left\{\sup_PQ_{P,1-\gamma}(|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)|)\right\}^2.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(\widetilde\theta\) and using the cited lower bound gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}
 \ge\gamma(\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G})^2
 \ge\gamma L_{\mathrm G,n,\gamma}^2.
\]
The bounded-outcome Gaussian class, the common codes, and the lower-quantile convention have remained unchanged throughout.
statements.justification: This theorem keeps the published bounded-outcome experiment and makes the quantile-to-MSE conversion explicit.
statements.gap: The published result is a generalized-quantile lower bound, not an MSE theorem on a conditional-sub-Gaussian outcome-noise class.
statements.consumer: The repaired common-code dichotomy can compare mean-squared errors without misrepresenting the Gaussian source theorem.

statements.statement: Fix the same deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), its clipped pair \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), and the same nested radii \((\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n})\) in both branches. Along every sequence of indices \(n\to\infty\) for which \(n\ge2\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\neq\varnothing\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), the separated non-Gaussian branch satisfies \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}\) for arbitrary \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\), including fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Separately, on the exact Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis bounded-outcome Gaussian branch, if \(0<\varepsilon_{1,n}<1\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\varepsilon_{2,n}=o\{(\log n)^{-1/2}\}\), then, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}\ge\gamma c_{\gamma}^2[\sigma^{-2}\varepsilon_{1,n}\varepsilon_{2,n}\{\log(1/\varepsilon_{1,n})/\log n\}^3+\sigma^{-1}n^{-1/2}]^2\).
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the proposed statement.  Along every indicated non-Gaussian sequence of indices, \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) gives fixed constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that
\[
 \frac cn\le\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le\frac Cn.
\]
The constants are uniform in \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\), and the only restriction on the treatment radius is \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\).  This proves \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\asymp n^{-1}\), including the admissible case of a fixed nonzero \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\).

Separately, for all sufficiently large indices satisfying the Gaussian hypotheses, \(\text{thm:gaussian-quantile-to-mse}\) gives
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}\ge\gamma L_{\mathrm G,n,\gamma}^2.
\]
Substitution of the displayed definition of \(L_{\mathrm G,n,\gamma}\) yields
\[
 \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}\ge
 \gamma c_{\gamma}^2\left[
 \sigma^{-2}\varepsilon_{1,n}\varepsilon_{2,n}
 \left\{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_{1,n})}{\log n}\right\}^{3}
 +\sigma^{-1}n^{-1/2}\right]^2.
\]
Both conclusions use the same deterministic supplied codes and radii, but they concern the two separately defined law classes; no equality or inclusion of those classes is asserted.
statements.justification: The same supplied information can have different minimax value depending on whether the treatment transform is zero-free or uniformly has a usable zero.
statements.gap: Published work supplies the Gaussian quantile barrier and finite-order non-Gaussian upper bounds, but not the exact spectral branch or its paired common-code MSE consequence.
statements.consumer: A structure-agnostic analyst can determine when an outcome code remains information-theoretically necessary after fixing the treatment-noise class.

statements.statement:
For every \(n\) such that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\), let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\). Suppose that \(\eta\sim\tfrac12N(-1,1)+\tfrac12N(1,1)\), \(\eta\perp X\), \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\) almost surely, \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\), \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\) almost surely, and \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\). Then \(\kappa_4(\eta)=-2\), \(M(i\pi/2)=0\), and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)\right]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P\!\left[\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)\right]
\ge \frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that, uniformly over all laws \(P\) satisfying the preceding conditions,
\[
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
No condition on the supplied outcome code or on \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) is required.
statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Proof.}
Put \(a=\pi/2\).  A random variable with the stipulated mixture law can be represented as \(\eta=R+E\), where \(R\) is Rademacher, \(E\sim N(0,1)\), and \(R\) and \(E\) are independent.  Therefore
\[
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}]=e^{z^2/2}\cosh z,
\qquad
M(ia)=e^{-a^2/2}\cos a=0.
\]
The variable \(\eta\) is centered, \(E_P[\eta^2]=2\), and
\[
E_P[\eta^4]
=E_P[(R+E)^4]
=E_P[R^4]+6E_P[R^2]E_P[E^2]+E_P[E^4]
=1+6+3=10.
\]
The fourth cumulant identity \(\kappa_4(U)=E[U^4]-3E[U^2]^2\) for a centered random variable now gives
\[
\kappa_4(\eta)=10-3\cdot 2^2=-2.
\]

We next establish the denominator identity and its boundary modulus.  The characteristic function of \(\eta\) is
\[
\phi(t)=E_P[e^{it\eta}]=e^{-t^2/2}\cos t.
\]
For every deterministic \(d\in\mathbb R\), symmetry of \(\eta\) and differentiation under the expectation, justified by the Gaussian-mixture moments, imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{t(\eta+d)\}]
&=-\frac{d}{dt}E_P[\cos\{t(\eta+d)\}]\\
&=-\frac{d}{dt}\{\phi(t)\cos(td)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\phi(a)=0\) and \(\phi'(a)=-e^{-a^2/2}\), evaluation at \(t=a\) yields
\[
E_P[(\eta+d)\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=e^{-a^2/2}\cos(ad).
\]
The independence condition \(\eta\perp X\), and hence independence of \(\eta\) and the \(X\)-measurable variable \(D_n\), permits conditioning on \(D_n\).  Since \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\), this gives
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(aZ_n)]
=e^{-a^2/2}E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
=e^{-\pi^2/8}E_P[\cos(\pi D_n/2)].
\]

By construction \(\bar g_n\) takes values in \([-C_g,C_g]\), and the treatment-regression range assumption gives \(|D_n|\le2C_g\) almost surely.  Because \(s\ge1\) and \(P_X\) is a probability measure, the treatment-code radius and H\"older's inequality give
\[
E_P|D_n|\le \|D_n\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
The elementary inequality \(1-\cos u\le |u|\) therefore implies
\[
E_P[\cos(aD_n)]
\ge1-aE_P|D_n|
\ge1-\frac{\pi}{2}\frac1\pi
=\frac12.
\]
Thus the certified population denominator lower bound is
\[
c_0:=\frac12e^{-\pi^2/8}>0.
\]
This is the required overlap, relevance, and division condition; the estimator's cutoff ensures that it never divides by an empirical denominator smaller than \(c_0/2\).

It remains to prove the uniform risk bound.  Define
\[
W_i:=Z_{n,i}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\qquad
V_i:=\{Y_i-\theta_0(P)Z_{n,i}\}\sin(aZ_{n,i}),
\]
and write \(\bar W_n=\mathbb P_nW\) and \(\bar V_n=\mathbb P_nV\).  From the definitions of \(b_n\), \(Z_n\), and \(\xi\),
\[
Y-\theta_0(P)Z_n=b_n(X)+\xi,
\qquad
b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)D_n.
\]
Also, for every \(d\),
\[
E_P[\sin\{a(\eta+d)\}]
=\operatorname{Im}\{e^{iad}\phi(a)\}=0.
\]
Consequently, treatment-noise independence gives
\[
E_P[b_n(X)\sin(aZ_n)]=0.
\]
Because \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) is measurable with respect to \((X,T)\), outcome mean independence gives
\[
E_P[\xi\sin(aZ_n)]
=E_P\!\left[E_P[\xi\mid X,T]\sin(aZ_n)\right]=0.
\]
Hence \(E_P[V_i]=0\).

All second moments used below are uniform.  Indeed, with
\[
b_{\max}:=C_q+2C_{\theta}C_g,
\]
the support conditions give \(|b_n(X)|\le b_{\max}\).  The conditional sub-Gaussian assumption implies \(E_P[\xi^2]\le K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2\) for an absolute constant \(K_{\xi}<\infty\) fixed by the convention for the \(\psi_2\)-norm.  Since \(|\sin u|\le1\),
\[
E_P[V_i^2]
\le2b_{\max}^2+2K_{\xi}\psi_{\xi}^2
=:K_V.
\]
Likewise,
\[
E_P[W_i^2]
\le E_P[Z_n^2]
\le2E_P[\eta^2]+2E_P[D_n^2]
\le4+8C_g^2
=:K_W.
\]
These bounds also verify every integrability condition used in the conditioning, differentiation, and variance steps above.

Let \(\mathcal A_n=\{\bar W_n\ge c_0/2\}\), the event on which the sample ratio is used.  On \(\mathcal A_n\), projection onto \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\) cannot increase distance from \(\theta_0(P)\), and therefore
\[
|\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P)|^2
\le \frac{\bar V_n^2}{\bar W_n^2}
\le \frac{4\bar V_n^2}{c_0^2}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_n^c\), both the clipped estimator and the target lie in \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\), so the squared loss is at most \(4C_{\theta}^2\).  If \(m_W=E_P[W_i]\), the denominator calculation gives \(m_W\ge c_0\); hence the independent and identically distributed sampling assumption and Chebyshev's inequality yield
\[
P(\mathcal A_n^c)
\le P\!\left(|\bar W_n-m_W|\ge\frac{c_0}{2}\right)
\le\frac{4\operatorname{Var}_P(W_i)}{nc_0^2}
\le\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}.
\]
The same sampling assumption and \(E_P[V_i]=0\) give
\[
E_P[\bar V_n^2]=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_P(V_i)}{n}\le\frac{K_V}{n}.
\]
Combining the regular and fallback events proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P))^2]
&\le \frac{4K_V}{nc_0^2}
+4C_{\theta}^2\frac{4K_W}{nc_0^2}\\
&=\frac{4K_V+16C_{\theta}^2K_W}{c_0^2}\,\frac1n.
\end{aligned}
\]
The displayed constant depends only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), not on \(P\), \(n\), the supplied outcome code, or \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\).  This establishes the asserted uniform root-\(n\) mean-squared-error rate, including all support, positivity, overlap, and boundary conditions.

statements.statement:
For \(n\ge2\), there is \(K<\infty\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and \(R_1\), such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) with \(|I_a|\ge1\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|^2\right]
 +E_P\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|^2\right]
 \le \frac{K}{|I_a|}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(m_a=|I_a|\) and let \(\mathbb P_a\) denote the empirical average on that half-sample.  Uniformly on \(|z|\le R_1\), the exponential series and the class moment bounds permit termwise subtraction:
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)
 =\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^m}{m!}(\mathbb P_a-P)Z_n^m,
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)
 =\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^m}{m!}(\mathbb P_a-P)(YZ_n^m).
\]
For every square-integrable \(W\), independence within the half-sample gives
\[
 \left\|(\mathbb P_a-P)W\right\|_{L^2(P^{\otimes m_a})}
 \le m_a^{-1/2}\|W\|_{L^2(P)}.
\]
The sub-Gaussian moment inequality, \(|D_n|\le2C_g\), and \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\) imply, for a class-uniform \(C<\infty\),
\[
 \|Z_n\|_{L^p(P)}\le C\sqrt p,
 \qquad p\ge2.
\]
Also \(Y=q_0(X)+\theta_0\eta+\xi\).  The boundedness of \(q_0\) and \(\theta_0\), together with the unconditional consequence of the conditional \(\psi_2\) bound on \(\xi\), gives \(\|Y\|_{L^4(P)}\le C\).  Hence
\[
 \|Z_n^m\|_{L^2(P)}\le(C\sqrt m)^m
\]
and, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \|YZ_n^m\|_{L^2(P)}
 \le\|Y\|_{L^4(P)}\|Z_n^m\|_{L^4(P)}
 \le C(C\sqrt m)^m.
\]
Minkowski's inequality now yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left\|\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)|\right\|_2
 &\le m_a^{-1/2}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}
   \frac{R_1^m(C\sqrt m)^m}{m!},\\
 \left\|\sup_{|z|\le R_1}|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)|\right\|_2
 &\le Cm_a^{-1/2}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}
   \frac{R_1^m(C\sqrt m)^m}{m!}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The series is finite by the ratio test, or directly from \(m!\ge(m/e)^m\).  Squaring both inequalities and enlarging the class-uniform constant proves the claim.  This argument also justifies all earlier termwise operations and introduces no entropy or logarithmic loss.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), the same externally supplied deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) is clipped and used in both branches; the pair may vary with \(n\) but is fixed before the independent inference sample is drawn.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment with the definitional residual \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\); the spectral branch imposes independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian noise, while the Gaussian comparator branch is exactly the known-variance bounded-outcome class of Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 3.2.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used; spectral relevance is a positive winding number with a boundary modulus bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The deterministic radii \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) are nonincreasing, so the uncertainty balls are nested. The spectral estimator uses only \(\bar g_n\); the Gaussian comparison uses the same clipped pair and radii.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.4, condition (21), and bound (22) give a \((1-\gamma)\)-quantile ACE error bound \(B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}\) over the published sub-Gaussian independent-noise uncertainty-class intersection.
Theorem 3.2 and equation (6) lower-bound generalized-quantile error over the bounded-outcome Gaussian PLM uncertainty class by \(L_{\mathrm G,n,\gamma}\).
A second-order orthogonal PLM moment exists if and only if the treatment residual is non-Gaussian under their regularity conditions.

tldr: Complex zeros of the treatment-noise moment generating function yield exact shift-annihilating instruments. With \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), the established identities \(F_n=M H_n\) and \(G_n=\theta_0F_n'+M B_n\) give an observable contour formula for \(\theta_0\). The flagship theorem target proves, through compact-open closure, a finite uniformly conditioned contour bank and a measurable split-sample selector with uniform MSE \(\Theta(n^{-1})\) whenever \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), including fixed nonzero treatment-code error and arbitrary outcome-code error. The same deterministic code sequences and nested radii feed an exact Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis bounded-outcome Gaussian branch, whose published generalized-quantile lower bound is converted explicitly to MSE. The resulting target is a Gaussian-versus-separated-non-Gaussian common-code dichotomy, with the local-to-Gaussian frontier left open.

project_justification.gap: Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Theorem 5.4 gives a finite-order ACE quantile upper bound, subject to condition (21), that retains treatment--outcome and treatment-only nuisance terms. Its Theorem 3.2 establishes the Gaussian quantile barrier on a different bounded-outcome class. Classical location-family theory recognizes transform zeros but does not convert learned-residual zero geometry into a causal estimator with uniform risk.
project_justification.niche: Independent cumulant-separated sub-Gaussian treatment noise creates a global null space for every location shift induced by treatment-code error. Small fixed residual contamination preserves this geometry, and observable contours avoid estimating the unknown noise law.
project_justification.fill: The project formalizes the exact annihilator and contour identities, proves zero localization and a finite uniformly conditioned contour bank, establishes selector measurability and uniform \(L^2\) empirical-process bounds, derives \(n^{-1}\) upper and lower MSE bounds, and states the Gaussian comparator on its exact published class with the quantile-to-MSE bridge shown.

related_work: \cite{Robinson1988} supplies the partially linear conditional-mean model. \cite{ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML} supplies orthogonal scores and sample splitting but ordinarily uses both nuisance regressions. \cite{MackeySyrgkanisZadik2018} establishes the finite-order non-Gaussian orthogonality frontier and informs the contrast with exact annihilation. \cite[Theorem 5.4, condition (21), and bound (22)]{JinMackeySyrgkanis2025} is the precise ACE comparator; \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) strictly tightens its eligible-sequence nuisance-order guarantee on the stated class intersection. \cite[Theorem 3.2 and equation (6)]{JinMackeySyrgkanis2025} supplies the bounded-outcome Gaussian generalized-quantile branch, which \(\text{thm:gaussian-quantile-to-mse}\) translates to MSE without equating that class to the non-Gaussian conditional-sub-Gaussian class. \cite{Mattner1992} is the classical location-family completeness background, not a theorem-level target. \cite{HuShiu2022} informs observable zero inheritance and pointwise real-zero testing. \cite{DinhGhoshTranTran2021} informs the Borel--Caratheodory and Cauchy zero-localization route. \cite{NeweyRobins2018} informs independent-fold evaluation, and \cite{ChackoViceira2003} is a complex-moment GMM precedent. \cite{LeeMesters2024} informs the weak-non-Gaussian open question. \cite{ReizingerEtAl2025} provides adjacent non-Gaussian treatment-effect motivation but does not subsume learned-residual contour adaptation.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact shift-annihilation, transform factorization, contour identity, nuisance-factor bound, and mixture algebra are established analytic reductions. The compact-open closure of the cumulant-separated MGF class, preservation of cumulant separation under that closure, uniform zero count and boundary modulus, measurable finite-bank selector, uniform \(L^2\) empirical-process bounds for \(e^{zZ_n}\) and \(Ye^{zZ_n}\), failure-event control, and common-code parametric lower-submodel membership remain proof obligations for the flagship theorem. No assumption substitutes for these obligations.
honest_scope: The proposal's headline \(C/n\) upper bound and matching \(c/n\) lower bound are theorem targets for D0, not verified results. The ACE comparison is restricted to indices satisfying the exact Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis condition (21), and \(s\ge r+1\) is used only to imply the required \(L^r(P_X)\) controls; it does not make the two base classes identical. The Gaussian MSE statement is only the explicit loss consequence of the published bounded-outcome quantile theorem. When \(\varepsilon_{1,n}=0\), the contour formula reduces to a known-residual location-family instrument; for the symmetric Gaussian mixture it reduces to the sine-score proposition. The shrinking-separation risk and coverage frontier remains open.
